battle.name: 解放者內戰
battle.brief: 公元前44年三月，凱撒在羅馬被布魯圖斯等「解放者」刺殺，奧克塔維安與安東尼組成三頭同盟追擊，戰火燒到馬其頓。公元前42年腓立比之戰，兩軍在安吉提斯河畔平原以方陣與投槍決戰，三頭同盟攻破其營地。卡面的亞述長矛成於公元前九百年，未曾現於此役，但其鐵葉形長矛傳統，正是兩軍步兵長矛的源流。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 交戰的兩大陣營都在羅馬共和國框架之內，卻彼此否認對方的合法性。解放者一方以恢復共和為名，集結執政官級別的元老派：布魯圖斯、卡西烏斯與德西穆斯·布魯圖斯，加上被放逐的元老與騎士階層，其基地在意大利以外——卡西烏斯在西班牙組軍，布魯圖斯在馬其頓的帖薩利與希臘城市徵集兵員，並僱用色雷斯人、蓋特人與葛利高利亞人充當輔助軍；德西穆斯則駐守山南高盧，握有經過實戰的隊伍。第二次三頭同盟一方是執政官安東尼、凱撒的法定繼承人奧克塔維安與非洲總督勒必達，三人依利克提亞法取得五年期、超越常設官制的非常權力，掌羅馬的稅收、城市徵召與退伍老兵資源。意大利的公民與退伍兵多站在三頭同盟一邊，因為安東尼在凱撒葬禮上的演說把死者描成受害者。區域性的第三力量在東地中海：克婁巴特拉七世的埃及與安東尼結盟，稍後收留布魯圖斯殘部的騎兵；帕提亞則趁羅馬內戰削弱安東尼，在高盧與西班牙扶植昆圖斯·拉比厄斯，使北意大利與西班牙戰線同主戰場一齊燃燒。
countriesEn: Both great camps fought inside the framework of the Roman Republic, and each denied the legitimacy of the other. The Liberators rallied the senatorial order at consular rank under the banner of restoring the Republic: Brutus, Cassius and Decimus Brutus, joined by exiled senators and equestrians, with their base outside Italy — Cassius raised an army in Spain, Brutus mustered men in Thessaly and in the Greek cities of Macedonia and hired Thracians, Getae and Galatians to serve as auxiliaries, while Decimus held Cisalpine Gaul with troops seasoned in real fighting. The other side was the Second Triumvirate: the consul Mark Antony, Caesar's legal heir Octavian, and Lepidus, governor of Africa. By the lex Titia the three took five years of extraordinary power beyond the normal magistracies, which gave them control of Roman taxation, the levy of the cities and the veteran manpower of the peninsula. Most Italian citizens and veterans leaned toward the triumvirs, because Antony's funeral oration for Caesar painted the dead dictator as the victim and the conspirators as his butchers. Two regional powers stood off the main line of the conflict: the kingdom of Cleopatra VII in Egypt, allied with Antony, which later took in the cavalry of Brutus's broken army, and Parthia, which used the Roman civil war to weaken Antony by backing Quintus Labienus in Gaul and Spain, so that the northern Italian and Spanish fronts burned at the same time as the main theatre.
people: 關鍵人物集中在執政官這個級別。凱撒在公元前44年三月十五日遇刺，他身兼終身獨裁官與執政官，是被刺殺的對象而非本役的指揮者。策動弒君的布魯圖斯事後出任公元前42年的執政官，駐軍馬其頓，風格穩重，主張以正面消耗取勝；卡西烏斯同為執政官，風格更銳利，在腓立比第一役靠色雷斯騎兵奇襲得手，第二役卻主張退守營地，突圍時自盡。德西穆斯·布魯圖斯最早接管山南高盧與西西里，因指揮保守被三頭同盟包圍，戰敗後被自己效忠的高盧首領殺死。奧克塔維安接下凱撒遺囑時只有十九歲，靠西西里的軍隊與老兵的忠誠迅速組軍，在穆蒂納初露鋒芒，後在布倫迪西與安東尼勉強會和，腓立比時指揮一翼。安東尼握有經驗、錢糧與東方人脈，卻在戰略判斷上屢次落後於奧克塔維安與阿格里帕。配角裡，色雷斯王子羅埃梅忒斯的騎兵在最關鍵時刻自行潰散；阿格里帕在海上以小型快船與登船橋擊敗塞克斯圖斯·龐培；昆圖斯·拉比厄斯在帕提亞支撐下於西班牙作戰，最終死在上多瑙山中。
peopleEn: The decisive figures all held the rank of consul. Caesar, who was stabbed on 15 March 44 BC while holding the office of dictator for life alongside his consulship, was the victim of the conflict rather than a commander in it. Brutus, who had set the assassination in motion, became consul for 42 BC and based himself in Macedonia; his style was deliberate and he argued for grinding the enemy down in a set-piece battle. Cassius, consul with him, was the sharper of the two: he won the first action at Philippi with a charge of Thracian cavalry, and at the second action urged a withdrawal into the camp, then killed himself when the line broke. Decimus Brutus took charge of Cisalpine Gaul and Sicily first of all, but his cautious command let the triumvirs close around him, and after his defeat he was killed by the Gallic chieftain who had served him. Octavian, who took up Caesar's will at nineteen years of age, built an army quickly out of the troops in Sicily and the loyalty of the veterans, showed himself at Mutina, met Antony grudgingly at Brundisium, and commanded one wing at Philippi. Antony held the experience, the money and the eastern connections, but was repeatedly out-thought in strategy by Octavian and Agrippa. Among the supporting cast, the cavalry of the Thracian prince Rhoemetes broke up at the decisive moment; Agrippa beat Sextus Pompey at sea with small fast ships and boarding bridges; and Quintus Labienus, backed by Parthia, campaigned in Spain before dying in the mountains of Raetia.
kits: 卡面這件亞述長矛是公元前九世紀兩河流域的產物：短柄、長刃、鐵製矛頭，形制接近狹長的葉片或柳葉，靠刺擊與推壓使用，與弓、投石索、鐵斧並列，是亞述密集方陣步軍的標準裝備之一。它不是任何羅馬部隊的編制裝備，公元前42年的馬其頓平原上不會出現這樣的兵器。但它代表一條延續了九百年的技術路線——早期鐵器時代那種窄葉鐵矛頭配長杆的近身刺擊兵器，經波斯、希臘與色雷斯一路傳到羅馬：共和國晚期的軍團步兵以標槍（長杆、鐵質矛頭，一次投射兩支）負責接戰前的距離消耗，以一把長矛作近身刺擊，主官另持無鏃的儀仗長矛，配短劍與盾牌。兩軍的輔助部隊顯示出多樣的地方裝備：色雷斯人的輕盾兵用小盾配色雷斯長矛，蓋特與西班牙的騎兵用短柄長矛配大盾，高盧與伊利里亞的輕步兵攜帶投石；安東尼與奧克塔維安的水師用多列槳的輕快戰船與五列槳大船，船上備有接舷用的木橋與甲板投石器。攻城與野營方面，羅馬式營地每日挖掘壕溝、豎立柵欄與拒馬，佩魯賈之圍用塔樓與封鎖線，海路運輸則靠上述戰船與輔助獸力。
kitsEn: The Assyrian spear on the card is a product of the ninth-century BCE riverlands: a short grip, a long blade and an iron head shaped close to a narrow leaf or willow leaf, used by thrusting and pressing rather than by swinging, and listed alongside the bow, the sling and the iron axe as standard equipment of the Assyrian close-order infantry. It was not part of the kit of any Roman unit, and nothing like it appeared on the Macedonian plain in 42 BC. What it does represent is a technical line running unbroken for nine centuries: the early-iron-age thrusting weapon of a narrow iron head on a long shaft, passed down through Persia, Greece and Thrace into Rome. In the late Republic the legionary fought with javelins — long shafts with iron heads, two of them thrown at the opening of the action — to wear down the enemy at range, kept a long thrusting spear for the close fight, and officers carried a plain parade spear without a head, together with a short sword and a shield. The auxiliaries on both sides show the diversity of local gear: Thracian peltasts fought with small shields and Thracian spears, Getae and Spanish horsemen carried short-hafted spears with large shields, and Gallic and Illyrian light infantry brought slings. At sea, Antony and Octavian used multi-banked light galleys and five-banked ships fitted with boarding bridges and deck-mounted stone throwers. For siege and camping, the Roman camp was dug and palisaded every evening, with a trench and a fence of stakes, the siege of Perugia used towers and lines of blockade, and sea transport ran on the same warships, with draft animals carrying the rest.
tactics: 腓立比在馬其頓東南、靠愛琴海的一片平原上，安吉提斯河與周邊沼澤橫在兩軍之間，限制了騎兵展開。奧克塔維安沿用凱撒式的三列縱深：前排輕裝步兵以標槍覆蓋敵陣、承受第一輪投射，第二排接上，第二排之後才是老兵與預備隊；縱深與密集旗幟使敵方的標槍與箭大量釘在盾牌上。兩翼配置騎兵，中央留出突破缺口。解放者的殺著是色雷斯與蓋特騎兵的衝鋒：第一役中對方騎兵衝破三頭同盟左翼，直抵敵營，解放者一度攻入並焚燒三頭同盟的營帳；同一批騎兵在隨後的混亂中自行潰散，營地得而復失。第二役三頭同盟以步兵正面纏鬥拖住解放者，再用預備隊與全線同時施壓，色雷斯、蓋特與希臘傭兵相繼逃散，解放者營地被攻破，軍隊崩潰。整場會戰是三段式：投射兵器、劍盾近戰、殘兵潰逃與投降。冬季的雨、泥濘與河岸的爛地同樣左右勝負，人馬一旦陷在泥裡，盾牌陣的推進就停了下來。往後戰場轉向兩個方向——佩魯賈的山地圍城考驗圍城器材與封鎖，海上的納烏洛庫斯與米拉萊兩役考驗船速、陣形與接舷：阿格里帕以小型快船保持編隊，避免被大船包抄，並在最後時刻放出登船橋，把火油與登船兵一起送上敵艦。
tacticsEn: Philippi lay on a plain in south-eastern Macedonia close to the Aegean, with the river Angitis and its marshes running between the two armies and restricting the deployment of cavalry. Octavian used the triple line devised by Caesar: light infantry in front covered the enemy and absorbed the first volleys of missiles, the second line followed, and seasoned veterans with the reserves stood behind that; the depth and the close-packed standards meant that the enemy's javelins and arrows were wasted on shields. Cavalry was posted on the wings with a gap left in the centre for a breakthrough. The Liberators' stroke was the charge of Thracian and Getic horse: in the first action the enemy horse broke through the triumviral left wing and rode straight to the camp, and for a time the Liberators were in and burning the triumviral tents; the same horsemen then scattered in the confusion and gave back what they had taken. In the second action the triumvirs pinned the Liberators in a frontal infantry fight, then applied pressure with the reserves along the whole line; Thracians, Getae and Greek mercenaries ran in turn, the Liberators' camp was stormed and their army collapsed. The whole engagement ran in three stages: missiles, then sword and shield at close quarters, then flight and surrender. Winter rain, mud and the boggy river banks mattered as much as the fighting; once horses and men were bogged down, the shield wall simply stopped advancing. Later the war moved in two directions — the hill siege of Perugia tested blockade works and siege equipment, while the actions off Naulochus and Mylae tested ship speed, line formation and boarding: Agrippa kept his small fast ships in order so they could not be enveloped by the heavier hulls, and at the last moment he cast his boarding bridges across, putting fire and boarders onto the enemy decks together.
data: 時間：公元前44年三月十五日凱撒遇刺，第二次三頭同盟於公元前43年成立，解放者主力在公元前42年十月的腓立比崩潰，餘波延續到公元前35年，整場戰爭橫跨約九年。清洗：公元前43年的首輪公職者名單包含約三百名元老與約二千二百名騎士，另有合計約三千人被列入通緝，各城設卡盤查，廣場按期重複宣讀名單。兵力：腓立比兩役的數字在古代記錄裡互相矛盾，通行說法是雙方各有兩萬至三萬人作戰，三頭同盟一方常被描述為擁有二十個軍團；共和國軍團在馬略改革後以十個步兵大隊組成，每大隊約六百人，一支滿編軍團連同輔助兵約五千人。損失與去向：布魯圖斯陣亡後，解放者軍隊約兩萬人投降，其後大批被編入三頭同盟軍隊；約三千名騎兵被送往埃及交給克婁巴特拉，日後悉遭處決。距離與地形：羅馬至布倫迪西的大道行程約九百公里，海軍再東行進入希臘；腓立比距卡瓦拉港約二十公里，營地就築在安吉提斯河旁的平原上；佩魯賈在翁布里亞的山丘之上，圍城拖到公元前39年；米拉萊在西西里東北岸。行軍：羅馬軍團每日推進約五至六公里，營地按羅馬式規制挖掘壕溝設柵。戰利品與土地：戰後解放者派系支持者的莊園與城市財產被沒收，用來安置退伍軍人，這筆土地成為日後意大利的主要爭端。
dataEn: Timing: Caesar was stabbed on 15 March 44 BC, the Second Triumvirate was constituted in 43 BC, the main Liberator force broke at Philippi in October 42 BC, and the aftermath dragged on to 35 BC, so the war as a whole spans roughly nine years. The purge: the first list of proscribed office-holders drawn up in 43 BC contained about three hundred senators and about twenty-two hundred equestrians, with roughly three thousand names in all marked for arrest, checkpoints set at the cities and the lists read aloud in the forum at intervals. Strength: the figures for the two actions at Philippi contradict one another in the ancient sources; the usual reckoning is twenty to thirty thousand men engaged on each side, and the triumviral side is commonly described as having twenty legions. After the Marian reforms a Roman legion was organised in ten infantry cohorts of about six hundred men each, so a full legion with auxiliaries came to roughly five thousand. Losses and disposal: after Brutus died, some twenty thousand of the Liberator troops surrendered, and large numbers were then taken into the triumviral armies; about three thousand horsemen were sent to Egypt and handed to Cleopatra, who had them all put to death. Distances and terrain: the road from Rome to Brundisium ran about nine hundred kilometres, and the fleet went on east by sea into Greece; Philippi lies about twenty kilometres from the harbour of Kavala, with the camps pitched on the plain beside the Angitis; Perugia stands on its hill in Umbria and its siege lasted into 39 BC; Mylae lies on the north-east coast of Sicily. Marching: a Roman legion advanced about five to six kilometres a day, digging and fencing the camp each evening by the Roman plan. Spoils and land: after the war the estates and urban property of the Liberators' sympathisers were confiscated and used to settle veterans, and that land became the standing quarrel of Italy in the decades that followed.
cause: 導火線是凱撒在共和國形式之下把權力集到底：他以終身獨裁官的身分掌握軍權、財權與立法權，接受國父與神化稱號，指定年輕的奧克塔維安為養子與繼承人，並把大量土地與公民權分給退伍軍人與被釋放的奴隸，元老派與保民派都在失去自主。執行刺殺的是一群自稱解放者的元老與騎士：布魯圖斯、卡西烏斯、德西穆斯與西梅等人，希望除掉獨裁者、恢復執政官與元老院的權力。但暗殺只解決了人，沒有解決權力的來源——凱撒的軍隊、地方城市與退伍老兵立刻轉向遺囑指定的繼承人，奧克塔維安憑合法性與金錢迅速集結軍隊，安東尼則用凱撒葬禮上的演說把民意扭轉過來；共和派匆忙組成的聯盟既無常備軍，也無法控制意大利城市的徵召，於是戰爭迅速從一場政變變成兩派對國家機器的爭奪。第二層原因在分配：土地法與退伍軍人安置的問題懸而未決，意大利公民對三頭同盟沒收敵產、重新分田的做法並不反感，這讓三頭同盟得以用財力換到兵源。東方與西方的邊界同時出問題，帕提亞趁亂扶植昆圖斯·拉比厄斯奪取西羅馬的殘餘勢力，戰線因此拉成三條。
causeEn: The trigger was the way Caesar concentrated power to the bottom under the shell of the Republic: as dictator for life he held the army, the treasury and the initiative in legislation, accepted the title of Father of the Country and divine honours, named the young Octavian his adopted son and heir, and distributed large tracts of land and citizenship to veterans and freedmen, so that both the senatorial and the popular factions were losing their independence. The assassins were a group of senators and equestrians who called themselves the Liberators — Brutus, Cassius, Decimus and Cimber among them — and hoped that removing the dictator would restore the consuls and the senate. But the assassination settled the man, not the source of power: Caesar's soldiers, the municipal communities and the veterans turned at once to the heir named in the will, Octavian raised an army quickly on the strength of that legitimacy and of money, and Antony turned public opinion with the funeral oration for Caesar. The hastily assembled Republican league had no standing army and no control of the levy of the Italian cities, so the coup quickly became a struggle between two camps for the machinery of the state. A second cause lay in distribution: the land laws and the settlement of veterans were left unsettled, and Italian citizens were not hostile to a triumviral policy of confiscating enemy estates and redistributing them, which let the triumvirs buy manpower with money. The eastern and western frontiers also came apart at the same time, Parthia using the confusion to sponsor Quintus Labienus in taking over what remained of the western Roman position, and the war was pulled out into three separate fronts.
impact: 這場戰爭把羅馬共和國的政治結構拆到底：公元前43年依利克提亞法成立的三頭同盟擁有五年非常權力，公職者清洗被寫進制度，元老院與公民大會只剩下形式，隨後又加演兩次。退伍軍人成為最深的裂痕——戰後沒收的莊園用來安置數萬名老兵，換來的是國家欠下的人情帳，意大利的無地者與退伍軍人問題此後百年間不斷重演，每一次都與土地再分配和軍人偏好捆在一起。東方的命運也由此決定：安東尼以統治東方取得財富與兵源，把希臘城市與行省收入羅馬版圖，卻用個人而非共和制度來支配它；克婁巴特拉與他的結合把埃及和東方推到與奧克塔維安對立的位置，終於引出公元前31年的亞克興海戰與公元前30年的亞歷山大戰役，帝制由那裡接上。西方方面，塞克斯圖斯·龐培的海上王國被拔除，西西里回到意大利，羅馬的海軍與地中海貿易從此統一。思想上，解放者被理想化：布魯圖斯成為後世反獨裁與共和派的象徵，2月17日與3月15日的解放日在歐洲政治文化中沿用逾千年；而三頭同盟式的非常統治、沒收與清算，也成為近代專制政府永遠的反面教材。
impactEn: The war pulled the political structure of the Roman Republic down to the studs: the Triumvirate created in 43 BC under the lex Titia held five years of extraordinary power, the purge of senators and knights was written into the machinery of the state, and the senate and the assemblies of the people kept nothing but their forms, with two further rounds of proscription to follow. Veterans became the deepest fissure: the confiscated estates were used to settle tens of thousands of old soldiers, and the state took on a debt of favour it could not discharge; the problem of landless Italians and of the soldiery was to recur for a century, each time tied to redistribution of land and to the preferences of the army. The fate of the East was settled here as well: Antony took wealth and troops by ruling the East, pulling the Greek cities and the eastern provinces into the Roman sphere while governing them personally rather than through republican institutions, and his union with Cleopatra pushed Egypt and the East into opposition with Octavian, until the battle of Actium in 31 BC and the Alexandrian war of 30 BC, and from there the imperial settlement. In the West the maritime kingdom of Sextus Pompey was torn down, Sicily returned to Italy, and the Roman navy and the Mediterranean trade were unified at last. In the realm of ideas the Liberators were idealised: Brutus became the emblem of later anti-autocracy and republicanism, and the days of 17 February and 15 March stayed in European political culture for more than a millennium, while the extraordinary government, confiscation and liquidation of the triumvirs remained the standing counter-example for modern despotism.
result: 腓立比兩役決定了馬其頓與整個東方的歸屬：第二次會戰解放者陣營被攻破，卡西烏斯先在混戰中自盡，布魯圖斯隨後在無人護衛的營地裡以短劍自刎，兩人的頭顱被送回羅馬；其軍隊約兩萬人投降，約三千騎兵被送交埃及，終被處決。前線方面，德西穆斯·布魯圖斯在公元前43年穆蒂納戰敗後被高盧人殺死，他的軍隊隨後被安東尼收編；盧基烏斯·安東尼在佩魯賈被圍數月，公元前39年開城投降，奧克塔維安把他推到母親朱莉婭·克婁巴特拉面前以羞辱他。海上，塞克斯圖斯·龐培在公元前36年的納烏洛庫斯被阿格里帕打敗，公元前35年在米拉萊附近被掃滅；支持解放者的昆圖斯·拉比厄斯也於同年死在上多瑙。最後，解放者一方再無可對抗的武力，第二次三頭同盟獨佔羅馬；但取勝的一派在公元前36年瓜分權力、罷免勒必達，安東尼取得東方，奧克塔維安保有意大利與西方，前者的東方體系與後者的意大利帝國在公元前31至前27年間相撞，奧古斯都的元首制隨之建立，共和國從此走入帝制。
resultEn: The two actions at Philippi decided the fate of Macedonia and of the whole East. In the second engagement the Liberator camp was stormed: Cassius killed himself first in the confusion, and Brutus followed, cutting his throat with a short sword in a camp that no longer had anyone to guard it; their heads were carried back to Rome, where they were displayed during the consulship. Some twenty thousand of their men surrendered, and about three thousand horsemen were handed over to Egypt, where they were put to death. On the other fronts Decimus Brutus was killed by a Gaul after his defeat at Mutina in 43 BC, and his army was then taken over by Antony; Lucius Antonius was shut in at Perugia for several months and surrendered the city in 39 BC, and Octavian paraded him before his mother Julia to humiliate him. At sea Sextus Pompey was beaten by Agrippa off Naulochus in 36 BC and destroyed near Mylae in 35 BC, while Quintus Labienus, who had kept up the Liberator cause, died in the same year in Raetia. In the end the Liberators had no armed force left to resist, and the Second Triumvirate held Rome alone; but the winners divided the power in 36 BC and removed Lepidus, Antony taking the East and Octavian keeping Italy and the West, and the eastern system of the one collided with the Italian empire of the other between 31 and 27 BC, so that the principate of Augustus was built and the Republic gave way to the Empire.
